final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest structural compatibility among the pool; removal of a head-domain glycan may expose the receptor-binding surface. Sequence-model support is moderate but mechanistic rationale is strong.
Maximum sequence-model plausibility and strong structural compatibility support this aromatic-preserving substitution near the C-terminal head region.
Also maximum sequence-model plausibility with good structural compatibility; ranked slightly below W503Y due to a lower structural score.

stop_reason.detail: Additional MSA or functional-annotation evidence is unlikely to change the top three given convergent structural and sequence-model support.

history.rationale: Removes the NDS N-glycan sequon near the receptor-binding region, potentially reducing steric shielding and improving ephrin-B2/B3 access.
N308 is part of an N-x-S/T glycosylation sequon; removing this glycan may expose the receptor-binding surface and enhance G-mediated entry.
Reasonable but not exceptional structural compatibility (0.579) and moderate sequence plausibility; zero evolutionary frequency at a fully covered position weakens confidence.
Removes the NQT N-glycan sequon in the C-terminal domain, which may expose additional receptor contact surface and enhance entry.
N459 is part of an N-x-T glycosylation sequon; glycan removal may improve receptor access, though distal effects are uncertain.

Strongest structural compatibility (0.850) among the pool, consistent with glycan removal in the head domain possibly exposing receptor-binding surface; MSA support is weak but low coverage limits negative weight.
Conservative aromatic substitution at a likely ephrin-binding pocket residue; smaller Phe may improve hydrophobic packing without disrupting key contacts.
W503 likely lies near the ephrin-binding interface; replacing with Phe preserves aromatic packing while removing a polar indole NH.
Also has maximum sequence plausibility (1.0) and good structural compatibility (0.792); ranked slightly below W503Y due lower structural score.
Alternative aromatic substitution at the same ephrin-binding pocket position; Tyr could introduce favorable H-bonding while retaining hydrophobic contact.
W503Y retains aromatic character but introduces a hydroxyl that may alter hydrogen bonding at the receptor interface.
Maximum sequence-model plausibility (1.0) and high structural compatibility (0.838) make this an attractive aromatic-preserving substitution near the C-terminal head region.
Removes a positive charge adjacent to the likely hydrophobic receptor-binding loop, possibly reducing electrostatic penalty in the ephrin interface.
K501 is adjacent to W503; charge removal could modulate ephrin binding affinity, but effect direction is uncertain.
Moderate structural compatibility (0.617) but lower sequence plausibility (0.4) and unclear mechanistic benefit from removing a positive charge near W503.
Neutralizes an acidic residue near a conserved loop; may reduce repulsion with negatively charged ephrin surface features.
D232 is in a surface loop; removing a negative charge may affect local electrostatics but is a lower-priority hypothesis.
Structural compatibility is poor (0.389) and there is no strong mechanistic argument that charge removal at this position improves entry; slight MSA support is insufficient.

rejection.reason: Structural compatibility is poor (0.389) and there is no strong mechanistic argument that charge removal at this position improves entry; slight MSA support is insufficient.

history.rationale: Polar-to-Ala substitution in a surface loop may relieve steric constraints and favor a receptor-competent conformation.
T229 is near a flexible loop; removal of a hydroxyl could alter loop dynamics, but impact on entry is unclear.
High sequence plausibility (0.720) and solid structural compatibility (0.722), but mechanistic link to improved entry is less direct than glycan-removal or aromatic-preserving mutants.
Removes a positive side chain near a loop region, potentially increasing conformational flexibility needed for fusion triggering.
K252 is outside known receptor-binding regions; charge removal likely has minimal entry benefit.

rejection.reason: K252 is outside known receptor-binding regions; charge removal likely has minimal entry benefit.

history.rationale: Conservative core-distal substitution may improve overall G stability and surface expression, indirectly increasing entry efficiency.
Conservative hydrophobic substitution unlikely to significantly change receptor binding or fusion triggering.

rejection.reason: Conservative hydrophobic substitution unlikely to significantly change receptor binding or fusion triggering.

history.rationale: Methionine-to-valine substitution in a structured region may enhance folding stability and G incorporation into functional glycoprotein complexes.
M279V is a conservative change with no clear mechanistic link to enhanced cell entry.

rejection.reason: M279V is a conservative change with no clear mechanistic link to enhanced cell entry.

history.rationale: N334 is part of an N-x-S sequon; removing this N-glycan may improve receptor accessibility analogous to N308Q/N459Q.
